summary: The second release: more capabilities, and fixes for the bugs found since 1.0.

highlights.title: Send to any OpenTelemetry endpoint
highlights.text: An OTLP destination sends logs, metrics or traces to any OTLP endpoint.

highlights.title: Take a protocol of your own
highlights.text: A socket receiver takes lines, length-prefixed binary messages or messages of a fixed size, over TCP, TLS or UDP.

highlights.title: Admit senders by their certificate
highlights.text: Name the senders a receiver admits by their certificate's fingerprint. With trusted authorities set, limit them to the host names their certificates are issued to.

highlights.title: Set log levels for the whole fleet
highlights.text: Set a default level on the leader, and override it for a class, a class and one type, or a service. Every worker takes a change with no restart.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: A new pipeline can propose a parser for Cisco ASA and FTD lines, which the new Grok pattern `CISCOASALINE` reads.

Add schema offers OCSF 1.3.0 beside 1.9.0, since Amazon Security Lake reads 1.3. It also offers a schema for the records of one OpenTelemetry signal, as an OTLP receiver gives them and the OTLP destination sends them.

Export a pipeline as a zip, with its tests and samples, and the routes, sources and destinations that run it if you choose, and import it on another leader. Untick any object you do not want to export or import. An import lets you keep or rename each object whose id is already taken there, and matches each secret and certificate it names to one there.
Save the output rows on screen as a sample. While the editor runs over a capture you have not saved, you can save that input as a sample too.
A viewer can read samples, run previews, start captures, and run the pipeline editor over a capture without saving it. Saving or deleting a sample and running tests still need an editor.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: `formatTime` writes a datetime as text in a `parseTime` format.
`readInt`, `readFloat`, `readBytes` and `unpack` read binary messages, and `writeInt`, `writeFloat` and `pack` write them. `indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `includes` find a byte or a run of bytes.
`indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `includes` take a starting position, as they do in JavaScript, and arrays gain `lastIndexOf`.

features.title: Sources
items: A socket receiver takes what senders send in a protocol of their own, over TCP, TLS or UDP: lines, length-prefixed binary messages, or messages of a fixed size.
The object store sources can read an object's records by a length prefix or a fixed size, as well as by lines.

A receiver under TLS can admit senders by their certificate's fingerprint, whoever issued it. With trusted authorities set, it can limit admission to certificates issued to the host names it lists (RFC 5425).
Capture as sent, under Advanced on a receiver's capture, keeps what its senders wrote before any framing, with each sender's address, and downloads as NDJSON.

features.title: Destinations
items: An OTLP destination sends logs, metrics or traces as OTLP/HTTP protobuf to any OTLP endpoint.
The S3 destination's page shows how to write to an Amazon Security Lake custom source, with each record filed under its own `eventDay`.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: A deployment that stops or is replaced first delivers what it holds, waiting up to 30 seconds. Each destination writes its open files at once instead of at its interval. Each receiver stops taking new data and passes on the records it already took. The receivers that take requests (HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus, Elasticsearch) answer 503, so their senders try again; S2S and Syslog over TCP stop reading; Syslog over UDP drops what arrives and counts it.

Set log levels for the whole fleet in Admin › System › Logging: a default level, and overrides for a class, a class and one type, or a service. Each worker takes a change at its next heartbeat, with no restart. `SMELTR_LOG_LEVEL` is now the level a process starts at, until the leader's levels reach it.
Each log line has a class, a type and a service, and Status → Logs filters by each.
The log records when each issue began and cleared, as class `status`, types `began` and `cleared`, whether or not anyone has the Issues page open.
An editor can lower a Rows below or above normal warning to info, or reset a source's history so its normal is learned again from then on.
On a 10-second or 1-minute chart, the expected band comes from how far the source's rate swung at that resolution on past days.
The Map places each pipeline and destination beside what it connects to, so fewer lines cross, and stacks sources or destinations only when their names share a prefix.
Every disabled button says why it is disabled when you point at it or press it.
The leader's log now names, for each capture, what the workers were asked to read.

features.title: Agent
items: Once a conversation outgrows the model's context, the agent can read back its older turns, by a range of turns or a search.
For a model that writes no summary itself, the leader asks it for one once a conversation gets long, even in the middle of a turn.
When the agent runs out of rounds of requests in a turn, it tells you where it stopped.
The agent can read the capture you have open, the models it can pick from and the warning metrics, and can create a key.
The Agent page opens from the agent panel, and the menu under a person's name no longer lists it.

fixes.title: Build pipelines
items: A new pipeline proposes a parser for a capture only when the parser reads 99% of its records.
Every saved sample deploys, whether or not a test names it.
The pipeline editor opens each pipeline on its own sample when you move from one pipeline to another.

fixes.title: Smeltr language
items: `true`, `false` and `null` before a dot are values: `true.toString()` no longer looks for a field named `true.toString`.
A variable first set to `null` or `[]` refuses a later write that cannot blend with the writes before it: `let l = []; l = "s";` no longer compiles.
A float result that is infinite or not a number is null, with an Overflow or NaN exception, as an integer that overflows is. A float literal too large to hold, such as `1e400`, does not compile.

fixes.title: Sources
items: A syslog receiver with a line breaker keeps every whole message it holds when a sender over TLS hangs up without closing TLS.

An HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus or Elasticsearch receiver answers a request as soon as it has received it, so its sender is not held while a destination writes its file. Receivers already deployed change too when the worker is upgraded. A worker that crashes loses the records its receivers answered but had not yet delivered. To answer only after every destination has the records, as before, turn on `answerAfterDelivery`.

A worker raises its open-file limit to the most its host allows when it starts, and its receivers share the connections over TCP that the limit leaves room for, after what the worker keeps for its destinations and files. When they hold that many, a new connection takes the place of the one idle longest on any receiver, if that one has been idle a minute. Otherwise the new one is closed. The Cluster page shows how many connections each worker may hold. `maxConnections` caps one receiver's connections. `maxConnectionsPerSender` caps one address's connections, and `idleTimeoutSecs` closes idle ones. An HTTP, HEC, OTLP, Prometheus or Elasticsearch receiver also closes an HTTP/1 connection that sends no request for 30 seconds, so a sender that keeps its connection open between requests opens a new one.

A syslog message larger than its receiver's message size is cut to that size and the connection reads on; before, the connection was closed. A larger datagram is cut too, where it was dropped. Every receiver takes messages or requests of at least 2048 bytes, and a saved size below that runs at 2048.

fixes.title: Destinations
items: Object store and table destinations write their files every five minutes unless set otherwise, where it was every minute; destinations already deployed change too when the worker is upgraded. A table destination's file interval can be up to an hour, where it was 240 seconds.

fixes.title: Run a fleet
items: A source's normal is learned only from times no warning about it held, so an outage no longer lowers it.
Lag climbing is judged on the highest lag of each five minutes, over thirty minutes, so it no longer raises and clears with each commit.
On Windows, a leader listening on `[::]` takes IPv4 too.

The leader sets how often its workers report, with `SMELTR_LEADER_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS`. A worker's own heartbeat interval does nothing now, and a worker that sets it in its file says at start that it can be removed.
Furthest from normal on the Status page ranks sources against the normal their warnings use.
The leader keeps working after an internal error part way through a request, where it used to fail later requests until it restarted.
The Map names each source and destination card by its type, as the Sources and Destinations pages do, where a syslog receiver read as HTTP.
A viewer can read the warning metrics for the worker groups it views; before, that needed an administrator.

fixes.title: Agent
items: Agent permissions keep "as every area" after Save; before, the area showed nothing.
Switching quickly between conversations no longer leaves the one you left on screen.
The agent panel's conversation list is disabled when there is no conversation to pick.

fixes.title: Security
items: A leader serving a stand-in certificate can rotate away from it; before, every rotation was refused until a restart, which did not help.
The update check sends the leader's operating system and CPU architecture beside its version.
The container image leaves out expat, which smeltr does not use.

summary: The first release. Build pipelines in a browser, test them on captured samples, review and deploy them as Git commits, and run them on a fleet of workers.

highlights.title: Send your SIEM only what you search
highlights.text: Drop the records nobody searches and the fields nobody reads before they are indexed, and send a full copy to cheaper storage. Your senders change only where they send.

highlights.title: Every source in one schema
highlights.text: Map each vendor's logs to ECS, OCSF or your own schema on the way in, and see where a pipeline's output does not match it, in the editor and in review.

highlights.title: Build on records from your own sources
highlights.text: Capture a sample from a live source, see what each step adds, changes or drops as you type, and save the result as a test.

highlights.title: Review every change before it runs
highlights.text: Each change is a Git branch. Review its diff and test results, then approve and deploy it. Any earlier version is one deploy away.

highlights.title: See where every record goes
highlights.text: Follow each source through its pipelines to its destinations, with throughput and warnings.

highlights.title: Check what you install
highlights.text: Every release comes with its SBOM, a CVE report and a STIG report. The source code is public.

features.title: Build pipelines
items: A pipeline editor that previews every step on sample records captured from a live source, as you type.
Steps: Parser (JSON, CSV, Key/value and Regex/Grok), Eval, Code, Drop, Rename, Remove, Lookup, Unroll, Call, If and Comment.
A CSV or Key/value Parser can leave out the columns or pairs it does not need and send the shorter line on in the same format. A skipped CSV column stays as an empty column; a skipped pair is gone.
Lock a preview as a test, and see after each save whether every test still gives its result.
Schemas: read ECS, OCSF, JSON Schema or a CSV of fields, see what a pipeline produces against them, and export an Elasticsearch mapping.

features.title: Smeltr language
items: A typed, JavaScript-like language, compiled to run on whole columns, not row by row.
A standard library for text, numbers, times, addresses, URLs, user agents and hashes.

features.title: Sources
items: Kafka and Event Hubs, with Avro read through a schema registry.
Object stores: S3 with SQS, Azure Blob with a queue, GCS with Pub/Sub, and listings of S3, GCS, Azure Blob and SFTP.
Receivers: HTTP, Splunk HEC and S2S, OTLP, Prometheus remote_write, syslog and the Elasticsearch Bulk API.
HTTP APIs, Okta's System Log, PostgreSQL and MySQL.

features.title: Destinations
items: Elasticsearch, Splunk HEC, HTTP, Prometheus remote_write and a Log Analytics workspace.
Kafka and Event Hubs, as JSON or Avro.
Object stores and SFTP as JSON, CSV, Avro or Parquet, and Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables.

features.title: Run a fleet
items: One leader manages any number of workers in groups. Every change is a Git commit you review and deploy, and roll back.
A map of sources, pipelines and destinations, with volume, lag and warnings.
A worker runs each deployment in a process it can end, so a deployment that hangs or will not stop never keeps it from taking the next one.
Each worker sizes itself to its memory.
The leader tells you when a newer release is out.

features.title: Security
items: Local, OIDC and key accounts, with roles per area. A key account is one a script calls the API as.
Workers enroll with a code and talk to the leader over mutual TLS. Certificates can come from ACME.
Credentials are kept encrypted in the leader, by name and version.
